summary: I sent the prompt exactly as written. The agent loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans and read the spec, the Services page and every vendor/kit component. It then wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md, a 377-line plan that builds the Deploys page from the kit (pageHeader, filterBar, selectField, dataTable, badge, emptyState). It did not copy the hand-written markup from Services. No repo files were changed. The agent asked no clarifying questions, so I never had to answer one.
reasoning: All four criteria pass, each checked against the session log, the plan file on disk and git status. The plan builds the table and the environment filter with the kit's dataTable and selectField, it lives in docs/hyperpowers/plans/, the writing-plans skill was loaded, and the working tree has no changes outside the ignored docs/ directory.

observations.description: The agent's summary flagged its choice openly: it built from the kit instead of copying Services, and offered to rewrite Task 1 to match Services if I preferred. That is good transparency.
The plan is not committed, and .gitignore excludes docs/hyperpowers/, so the plan file is effectively invisible to git. The agent did mention this.

The skill tried to run a Codex review preflight, but the Codex plugin isn't installed. The agent recorded the skip in an 'ungated-ledger' script, and its message ended with a stray-looking '/codex:setup' line. That is noise for a user who only asked for a plan.
The agent made two decisions the spec doesn't cover and reported both: a 'No deploys' message when the snapshot is empty, and a descending default when ?sort is given without ?dir.
Two of the startup dialogs (workspace trust and bypass-permissions) have 'No, exit' selected by default, so pressing Enter quits. This is standard Claude Code behaviour, but testers can trip on it.

criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use: {"name":"Skill","s":"hyperpowers:writing-plans"}; screen: "Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill"

criteria.criterion: Plan's page code calls dataTable and selectField, with no hand-written <table>/<select>
criteria.evidence: The plan's code for src/pages/deploys.js imports `import { selectField } from '#kit/select'; import { dataTable } from '#kit/table';` and calls `selectField({ name: 'env', ... })` and `const table = dataTable({ columns: [...], rows: deploys, ... })`. I grepped for `<table` and `<select`. They only appear in the test assertions (lines 142 and 153), never in the page code (lines 170-240).

criteria.criterion: No implementation: no source, test, data, public or vendored file and not package.json created or changed
criteria.evidence: `git status --short --ignored` lists only `!! docs/`, which is ignored and holds the plan. `git diff --stat` is empty. The agent ran the plan's code in a `mktemp -d` copy made with `git archive`, not in the working tree.
